summary: The contract requires the promise to remain pending for the requested duration m, imposing a matching elapsed-time lower bound, while one host timer reaches that bound with constant JavaScript scheduling work.

optimality.argument: A valid promise cannot complete materially before the requested m-millisecond interval, so its elapsed completion time is Omega(m). Scheduling one host timer resolves it after approximately m milliseconds, giving O(m) elapsed time while performing only O(1) JavaScript work.

replacement_checks.evidence: Resolving materially before m milliseconds would directly violate the required sleep interval, establishing the elapsed-time lower bound.
One setTimeout registration invokes the promise resolver after the host timer reaches the requested delay, with no polling loop.
Cases exercise the 1-millisecond minimum, the 1000-millisecond maximum, both public examples, and an odd intermediate duration.
